messages:
michael: Heads-up — private customer reported cross-tenant routing when using a private endpoint + custom host header. They saw requests from ws-123 hit the shared pool instead of the dedicated one. Repro steps attached below.

anna: ouch. do we have a clear ordering for route matching today? gateway -> host -> header -> path?

sara: current flow is host header first (for legacy hostnames), then vhost rules, then long tail header rules. that order was to preserve existing tenant hostnames but i agree it's risky for VPC/private endpoints.

michael: repro: curl against vpce endpoint with X-Workspace-ID: ws-123 and Host: api.redwood.example.com routed to shared pool. we expect: if X-Workspace-ID maps to a dedicated pool -> short-circuit and route there.

infra-bot: deploy-check: gateway routing config last changed in 1767180000 by anna. no canary rollouts active.

anna: thinking out loud — two safe approaches:
1) Enforce workspace-scoped routing as the first priority for private endpoints (header or cert mapping), i.e. evaluate X-Workspace-ID before host rules when X-Private-Endpoint present.
2) Require strong auth for private endpoints (mTLS or signed token) and verify tenant identity at connection time; then we can use that identity for routing.

sara: both make sense. option 1 is faster but we must mitigate header spoofing. option 2 is more secure but needs infra (mTLS) and onboarding.

michael: agree. proposal: default behavior for private endpoints = enforce tenant scoping at gateway. Implementation details:
- If request contains X-Private-Endpoint header (or origin IP in vpce CIDR), evaluate tenant-scoping rule first.
- Tenant mapping sources: X-Workspace-ID (explicit), client cert CN (if present), and token claim (if present).
- If mapping yields a dedicated pool -> route to that pool. If mapping missing and workspace has "allow-fallback-to-shared" = false -> 403.
- For backwards compat, a per-workspace console flag "Enforce private routing" default = OFF, roll to opt-in customers, then flip on for paid Dedicated customers.

anna: config sketch (gateway matching DSL):
```yaml
routes:
  - name: tenant-scoped
    when: any( header(X-Private-Endpoint), ip_in_range(remote_addr, "10.240.0.0/16") )
    match:
      - header: X-Workspace-ID
        type: exact
    action:
      type: tenant_route
      tenant_header: X-Workspace-ID
      on_no_match: check_console_flag_or_fallback

  - name: host-fallback
    match:
      - host: api.redwood.example.com
    action: host_route
```

sara: also need to log events for telemetry: routed_to_dedicated_pool (tenant_id, pool_id, match_source), isolation_blocked (tenant_id, ip, reason), spoof_attempts (tenant_id, header_value, signature_ok=false).

devex-lead: UX notes: console should expose per-workspace setting, plus a rollout history and a "simulate" mode so ops can test without blocking. Can we surface which source matched (header vs cert) in the rollout dashboard?

michael: yes — telemetry tag match_source will drive UI badge (header/cert/token/ip). For rollout we need a canary percent and a list of tenant IDs included.

ops: quick security catch — X-Workspace-ID is trivially spoofable unless we require one of: mTLS cert mapping, signed header (edge-signed), or ephemeral token from control-plane. Otherwise attackers on same VPC could craft header.

anna: agree. minimum: accept header only if it's accompanied by a signed signature header from the VPC edge: X-Edge-Sig. Example handshake: control-plane issues per-vpce signing keys. Edge adds X-Edge-Sig that gateway verifies against known key for that vpce. If missing, treat header as untrusted.

michael: that's reasonable. combine with a conservative default: if header untrusted and workspace has dedicated pool -> route to shared and emit isolation_blocked. If workspace has forbid-fallback -> return 403.

sara: implementation tasks I see:
- gateway: add tenant-first matching when vpce flag present + signature verification (infra work)
- control-plane: per-vpce signing keys + rotation endpoints
- console: per-workspace toggle + simulate mode + rollout controls
- monitoring: new metrics + dashboards + alerts for isolation_blocked spikes

devex-lead: also add docs + migration guide. want a short blurb for customers: what to expect, how to enable, and how to provide their vpce signing key to support.

michael: can we agree on a minimal rollout plan? my proposal:
1) Build signature verification + tenant-first rule behind a feature flag in gateway (non-blocking, just tag events).
2) After 1 week of telemetry and no false positives, enable simulate mode for selected customers (console toggle).
3) After customer opt-in and testing, flip enforce=true for those customers (canary).
4) Default enable for Dedicated customers after 30d and then global flip for private endpoints 90d after.

anna: sounds good. i'll open an RFC and owner it. sara to spike signature verification proto. devex-lead to draft console spec. ops will create alert.

sara: spike notes: verifying X-Edge-Sig will require adding a small crypto lib to gateway (ed25519). sample verify call:
```go
ok := ed25519.Verify(pub, payload, sig)
if !ok { emitMetric("spoof_attempts", labels) }
```

infra-bot: ticket created: GATEWAY-1425 (tenant-scoped routing behind feature flag). assigned to sara.

michael: thanks. priority P1 for private customers. I'll follow up with the affected customer and update this thread with test results. :thumbsup:

ops: note — add a security alert if isolation_blocked > 5% of requests for a tenant for >10m.

michael: adding to action items. tagging @sara @anna @devex-lead for next steps.
